messages:
maria: quick thread — after yesterday's kernel swap we saw a small but consistent tail uplift for mixed long/short traffic. baseline 95p went from 120ms -> 210ms for some tenants. profiling + notes below.
kevin: which swap specifically? the fp16 fused-attn->new-kernel-v2?
maria: yeah that one. tail only shows up under continuous batching when short seqs intermingle with long ones. short-only workloads fine.
ravi: saw alerts on tenant:alpha at 03:12 UTC, queue backlog spiked. I grabbed a perf profile and a p99 trace.
li: key suspicion: kernel v2 has slightly worse kernel-launch overhead for small slices and changes the cost model used by the batcher kernel selector, so batch formation is skewed.
sophia: do we have kv-cache metrics for those tenants? maybe cache thrash amplified long windows -> low kv-hit-rate -> longer decode steps
maria: yes — tenant:alpha kv-hit-rate dropped ~7% correlating with tail spikes. hypothesis: batcher delays cause larger mini-batches that evict warm KV entries, then long sequences suffer.
perf-bot: uploaded traces to /artifacts/1765123456/{pprof,nvprof,flame} and started canary A/B (50/50) between kernel-v1 and kernel-v2 for 2h.
kevin: I ran an experiment locally with a toy mix: 80% short (16 tokens), 20% long (512 tokens). Observed that the continuous-batcher window_ms default (12ms) coalesced too many short reqs behind a long seq arriving first.
li: suggestion: bias batch formation to prefer homogeneous length grouping when possible. two simple levers: 1) max_mixed_batch_fraction (avoid >X% long tokens in same batch) 2) token_budget_target per tenant.
maria: also tried toggling kv.coalesce=true (backend flag) which coalesces KV writes across mini-batches. kv.coalesce reduced eviction churn and improved kv-hit-rate by ~4% in canary.
ravi: actionable checklist I propose:
  - run a micro A/B that toggles batcher.token_budget_target from 4096 -> 2048 for heavy-imbalance tenants
  - try batcher.homogenize_enabled=true (prefer same-seq-length grouping) for 10 tenants
  - enable kv.coalesce on canary hosts and measure kv-hit-rate + tail
  - add per-tenant deficit aging to avoid long tenants hogging credits for long windows
kevin: code snippet I used to repro (local loadgen):
```
loadgen --mix "short:80:16,long:20:512" --concurrency 200 --ramp 30s --duration 5m
# batcher overrides
BATCHER_WINDOW_MS=12
TOKEN_BUDGET_TARGET=4096
```
li: metric targets for success: 95p latency back within 10% of v1 and kv-hit-rate within 2% of pre-swap baseline. also ensure throughput token/sec within 5% of baseline.
sophia: one weird detail: kernel-v2 gives slightly better GPU SM util for pure-long workloads. so we can't just revert globally. need routing policy: route long-only traffic to v2, mixed to v1, or use adaptive batcher.
maria: agreed. propose a short-term mitigation: per-tenant routing rule based on recent seq-length distribution (if >80% long -> v2, if mix -> v1). medium-term: improve kernel selector by incorporating batch heterogeneity penalty in cost model.
ravi: telemetry additions: add a small histogram for batch heterogeneity (entropy of seq lengths inside batch) and kv-eviction-rate per minute. that will help correlate.
kevin: experiment notes: when I lowered TOKEN_BUDGET_TARGET -> 2048 for mixed load, 95p dropped back to ~130ms and kv-hit-rate recovered. downside: throughput dropped ~6% but acceptable for those tenants.
li: potential algorithm: dynamic_token_target = clamp(base_target * (1 - heterogeneity_score), min, max). simpler: maintain two token targets and pick based on recent heterogeneity window.
maria: let's run the following canaries today:
  - canary A: batcher.homogenize_enabled=true on 10% traffic (mixed tenants)
  - canary B: token_budget_target=2048 for 10% traffic
  - canary C: kv.coalesce=true on backend hosts for 10% of capacity
please record p95/p99, kv-hit-rate, tokens/sec, GPU util and batch_entropy every minute.
sophia: I'll patch routing to support seq-length based split for short-term routing to v1/v2.
kevin: one more thing — I profiled kernel launch times and v2 has +0.8ms per-launch for slices <32 tokens. that explains short penalty. maybe we can special-case short-slice path to use legacy small-slice kernel.
maria: nice. assign owners: kevin -> small-slice fallback PR, li -> cost-model change for kernel selector, ravi -> telemetry + canary dashboards, sophia -> routing split. I'll own kv-coalesce measurement.
perf-bot: TODOs created: #4321 small-slice-fallback, #4322 kernel-selector-costmodel, #4323 canary-telemetry, #4324 routing-seqlen-split
kevin: timeline: quick PRs for canary today, if results positive roll to 50% tomorrow and consider global rollout with selective routing.
maria: thanks all — let's sync tomorrow 10:30 for results. ping me @maria if something flames overnight.
